components.name: Slab Button
components.description: The one custom button style: clock-white slab, black label, presses down. One per screen, in the bottom safe-area bar or inset, with the text button under it.
components.css: .ds-slab-wrap { background: #0B0D10; padding: 12px 24px 8px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; } .ds-slab { display: block; width: 100%; min-height: 56px; border: none; border-radius: 12px; background: #F2F2EE; color: #0B0D10; font: 600 17px/22px -apple-system, system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 0.12s ease-out, opacity 0.12s ease-out; } .ds-slab:hover { opacity: 0.95; } .ds-slab:active { transform: scale(0.98); opacity: 0.85; } .ds-slab:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #F2F2EE; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-textbtn { width: 100%; min-height: 44px; border: none; background: none; color: #F2F2EE; font: 400 17px/22px -apple-system, system-ui, sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; cursor: pointer; } .ds-textbtn:hover { opacity: 0.8; } .ds-textbtn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #F2F2EE; outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 12px; }

components.css: .ds-cards { background: #0B0D10; padding: 16px 20px; display: flex; gap: 12px; font-family: -apple-system, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-card { flex: 1; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; padding: 14px; border: none; border-radius: 12px; background: rgba(242,242,238,0.08); text-align: left; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.12s ease-out; } .ds-card:hover { background: rgba(242,242,238,0.11); } .ds-card:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #F2F2EE; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-card-top { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; color: #8A8F98; font: 600 15px/20px inherit; } .ds-card-time { color: #F2F2EE; font: 600 34px/41px -apple-system, system-ui, sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-card-cap { color: #8A8F98; font: 400 12px/16px -apple-system, system-ui, sans-serif; }

components.css: .ds-chips { background: #1C1C1E; padding: 12px 16px; display: flex; gap: 6px; border-radius: 26px; } .ds-chip { flex: 1; min-height: 44px; border-radius: 12px; border: 1.5px solid transparent; background: rgba(242,242,238,0.04); color: #8A8F98; font: 600 15px/20px -apple-system, system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; } .ds-chip.on { background: rgba(242,242,238,0.16); border-color: #F2F2EE; color: #F2F2EE; } .ds-chip:hover { background: rgba(242,242,238,0.08); } .ds-chip.on:hover { background: rgba(242,242,238,0.2); } .ds-chip:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #F2F2EE; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.css: .ds-field-wrap { background: #0B0D10; padding: 24px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 20px; } .ds-answer { width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; padding: 14px; border: none; border-radius: 12px; background: rgba(242,242,238,0.08); color: #F2F2EE; caret-color: #F2F2EE; text-align: center; font: 400 28px/34px -apple-system, system-ui, sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-answer::placeholder { color: #8A8F98; } .ds-answer:focus-visible { outline: none; background: rgba(242,242,238,0.12); } .ds-feedback { margin: 0; text-align: center; color: #8A8F98; font: 400 17px/22px -apple-system, system-ui, sans-serif; }

components.name: Station Dial
components.description: Signature: 60 bar indices (white majors, graphite minors), the red signal disc parked at twelve while latched, the sounding ring's tick in red. Hover shows the release: the disc swings 110 degrees clockwise and fades.
components.css: .ds-dial-wrap { background: #0B0D10; padding: 24px; display: flex; justify-content: center; } .ds-dial { position: relative; width: 200px; height: 200px; } .ds-dial::before, .ds-dial::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: 50%; } .ds-dial::before { background: repeating-conic-gradient(from -0.5deg, #8A8F98 0deg 1deg, transparent 1deg 6deg); -webkit-mask: radial-gradient(closest-side, transparent 89%, #000 89.5%, #000 96%, transparent 96.5%); mask: radial-gradient(closest-side, transparent 89%, #000 89.5%, #000 96%, transparent 96.5%); } .ds-dial::after { background: repeating-conic-gradient(from -1.5deg, #F2F2EE 0deg 3deg, transparent 3deg 30deg); -webkit-mask: radial-gradient(closest-side, transparent 76%, #000 76.5%, #000 96%, transparent 96.5%); mask: radial-gradient(closest-side, transparent 76%, #000 76.5%, #000 96%, transparent 96.5%); } .ds-tick { position: absolute; left: 50%; top: 13.5%; width: 5%; height: 10%; background: #E1251B; transform-origin: 50% 365%; transform: translateX(-50%) rotate(135deg); } .ds-signal { position: absolute; inset: 0; z-index: 1; transition: transform 0.5s cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.2, 0.64, 1), opacity 0.5s ease-out; } .ds-signal span { position: absolute; background: #E1251B; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%); } .ds-stem { top: 27.5%; height: 45%; width: 1.25%; } .ds-disc { top: 15%; width: 12%; height: 12%; border-radius: 50%; } .ds-hub { top: 48%; width: 4%; height: 4%; border-radius: 50%; } .ds-dial:hover .ds-signal { transform: rotate(110deg); opacity: 0; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-signal { transition: opacity 0.2s ease-out; } .ds-dial:hover .ds-signal { transform: none; opacity: 0; } }

narrative.overview:
Wakelatch is a Swiss railway clock in a dark room. The red second hand on those clocks pauses at twelve and waits for the signal before it moves on. Wakelatch is that pause: a latched alarm keeps ringing until the user gives the signal by finishing the challenge, and then the red disc swings away. Everything else on screen is the clock's enamel, its white bar indices and its graphite minor marks.

The app is dark-only. Every scene it serves happens in a dark room: setting tomorrow's two times at night, leaving the phone on the charger in bedside mode, and stopping the ring in the morning with bleary eyes and one hand. Screens are sparse and high-contrast: white on near-black, one dial, one sentence, one white slab at the bottom. Native SwiftUI structure (NavigationStack, inset grouped lists and forms, system toolbars and sheets, the wheel and compact time pickers, the system number pad) carries the app; the world lives in the colours, the dial, the large tabular numbers and the single slab. The direction refuses sunrise gradients, neon-on-black and the stock alarm list.

The world is flat. There are no custom shadows or gradients; depth comes from the system's grouped-list, toolbar and sheet materials, and from clock white at stated opacities sitting on enamel.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-only: enamel ground everywhere, pure black at the bedside.
One recurring form: the bar-index station dial, at every size from 96pt to full width.
Signal red means "latched" and nothing else, and is never text.
SF Pro only; tabular digits on every number; the big clock and count numbers scale with Dynamic Type up to a cap.
One radius (12pt) and one custom button (the slab), one slab per screen at the bottom.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal red means "latched" and nothing else: the disc while a latch is armed or holding, and the tick of the ring sounding now. It is never used for text.

rules.name: The Destructive Exception Rule
rules.body: Destructive buttons ("Skip this morning") keep the system red that `role: .destructive` gives them. This is a deliberate exception to the Signal Rule, following the HIG convention for destructive actions. Do not restyle them in signal red, and do not use the system red anywhere else.

rules.name: The Quiet Error Rule
rules.body: Errors and warnings are a `Label` in clock-face white with the `exclamationmark.triangle` symbol. Never red.

rules.name: The Dark Room Rule
rules.body: The app is dark-only (`.preferredColorScheme(.dark)` at the root, on the morning screens and on the skip sheet). Do not add a light appearance.

rules.name: The Bedside Black Rule
rules.body: Bedside mode alone uses a pure black ground. Its clock group (dial, time, first-ring line) is dimmed as one layer (`compositingGroup()` then 55% opacity) so overlapping strokes do not show through each other; the exit line underneath stays full graphite so it stays legible.

rules.name: The Timetable Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change (times, ring counts, problems, answers, step and shake counts) uses tabular digits, so values never jitter as they update.

rules.name: The Scaled Clock Rule
rules.body: Type is set with Dynamic Type text styles. The three big numbers are the only fixed-size sets, and each is a `@ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .largeTitle)` with a cap: 72 to 110, 64 to 96, 96 to 140. No custom fonts.

rules.name: The One Slab Rule
rules.body: Each screen has at most one white slab, and it lives in a bottom safe-area bar or inset, never in scrolling content.

rules.name: The Fits Above the Keys Rule
rules.body: At any Dynamic Type size, the math challenge shows its problem and answer field above the number pad. Shrink the dial first.

rules.name: The Enamel Rule
rules.body: Custom surfaces are enamel, clock white, or clock white at a stated opacity. No shadows, no gradients.

dos: Do keep every screen dark: enamel ground, `.preferredColorScheme(.dark)`; pure black only at the bedside.
Do reserve signal red for the latch: the disc and the tick of the ring sounding now.
Do show errors as a clock-white `Label` with `exclamationmark.triangle`.
Do leave destructive buttons in the system red of `role: .destructive`, per the HIG.
Do give every changing number tabular digits, and size the big clock and count numbers with `@ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .largeTitle)` and a cap.
Do put the one slab in a bottom safe-area bar or inset with a soft scroll edge behind it.
Do use the slab for the primary action and system styles, tinted clock white, for everything else.
Do use the 12pt radius and clock white at a stated opacity for any new custom surface.
Do write morning copy as short statements of fact: "Ring N of M. Deadline h:mm.", "Snooze until h:mm".
Do shrink the dial (96pt on the challenge) at accessibility sizes before dropping content.
Do pair the release with the success haptic and give it a crossfade under Reduce Motion.
donts: Don't use signal red for text, errors, buttons, badges or decoration.
Don't add a second custom button style or a second radius.
Don't bring in a custom typeface or set uncapped, unscaled point sizes.
Don't add shadows or gradients; the world refuses sunrise gradients and neon-on-black.
Don't replace the dial with the stock alarm list.
Don't put a slab inside scrolling content or place two slabs on one screen.
Don't set a custom AlarmKit sound.
